title: Points Ledger Accounting Note: Taking Back Points on Returned Merchandise under the Belrose Circle Membership Programme
content:
# Points Ledger Accounting Note — Taking Back Points on Returned Merchandise (Belrose Circle Membership Programme)

Points earned under the Belrose Circle Membership Programme on a sale are taken back when the merchandise is returned, in the same number they were earned in. The number of calendar days in the reversal window is fixed by the member's tier.

## Entries and their binding

Points are taken back only against the earning entry they answer, identified by the till transaction number and the earning entry the points were credited on. The binding is established from the ledger held by the company before the reversal is booked: the till transaction number on the return is matched to the earning entry that carries the same till transaction number on the same membership, and the reversal is booked against that entry and no other. A return whose till transaction number matches no earning entry on the membership has no earning entry to answer, and no points are taken back against it.

A reversal is recorded as one entry per return taking back the points earned on one sale, carrying the date the points were taken back, the points taken back as a negative figure, the spend given back as a negative figure, the till transaction the return answers, the earning entry being taken back and the accounting period the reversal is accounted to.

## The reversal window

Points are taken back only within the tier's reversal window in calendar days, counted from the date the sale the points were earned on was rung. The reversal window is counted in whole calendar days from the day of sale, that day counting as day zero, weekends and store holidays included. The date the sale was rung is read from the earning entry booked on that till transaction. A return dated on or before the last day of the window is within it; a return dated after that day is outside it, and no points are taken back on it.

### Counting the window (hypothetical dates)

Assume a tier whose reversal window is 90 calendar days, and a sale rung on 1 March of a non-leap year.

| Day of the return | Days counted from the day of sale | Within the window |
|---|---|---|
| 1 March | day zero | yes |
| 31 March | day 30 | yes |
| 30 April | day 60 | yes |
| 30 May | day 90 | yes, the last day of the window |
| 31 May | day 91 | no |

A Saturday, a Sunday or a store holiday falling inside the count is counted like any other day.

## Effect on the balance and on qualifying spend

Where the points earned on the sale have already been spent, the balance is allowed to go negative, and the member earns nothing further until it is back above zero. A reversal reduces the qualifying spend for the membership year as well as the balance, so a return can move a member back below a tier threshold.

### Effect illustrated (hypothetical figures)

A sale that earned 2469 points on USD 1234.56 of qualifying spend is returned within the window: 2469 points are taken back and USD 1234.56 is deducted from the qualifying spend of the membership year. If the balance before the reversal stood at 1000 points, it stands at 1469 points below zero afterwards, and nothing further is earned until it is back above zero.
